courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Combining theory and practice, this course will provide students with the ability to apply safe work practices on the job-site. Students will control workplace hazards, and apply Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and Workers Compensation Standards. They will learn and use the Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System. Students will learn to select and use personal protective equipment. They will learn to identify fire hazards, learn how to prevent fires and how to select appropriate fire extinguishers for the various types of fires. Students will also learn how to use tools and the many types of pipe used in the piping trades. Students will learn to select and use appropriate tools as well as inspect and maintain them. Students will first be introduced to hand tools and then to portable and stationary power tools. The major focus will be practical projects designed to challenge students in laying out and joining a variety of different types of pipe for different applications. Students will also learn how to test integrity of their piping installations. Students will learn how to select and use soldering materials and equipment appropriate to the piping process. Students will learn how to inspect and maintain soldering equipment. Students will be taught about the many fittings and connections used in the piping trades. They will learn how to select the appropriate fitting for the application and how to properly install and test these fittings. Students will learn how to erect and use ladders and elevated platforms. Students will use hoisting, lifting and rigging equipment. They will learn how to select and use knots, bends and hitches appropriate to the application. Math and science will be applied to piping applications. Students will apply math and science to understand the design and operation of drain, waste and venting systems, steam heating systems, hot water heating systems, potable water systems, and some residential gas systems. Students will be taught the principles of electricity as they apply to the piping trades. Pressure measuring tools will be described and applied to their piping projects. Drafting projects will be used to teach students how to use drafting tools. They will learn how to use drafting symbols, lettering, and line construction. Students will learn to interpret information found on a set of drawings and apply this information to their practical projects in the shop. They will learn the purpose of using different types of drawings to best convey information and to convert between isometric and orthographic drawings. Students will learn how to select and install pipes, valves, and fittings for a variety of piping systems. They will be taught how to properly penetrate structures without compromising the integrity of other building systems. Students will learn about different types of pumps used in the piping trades, how they work, and for which applications each type is best suited. Through practical projects they will learn how to install and maintain pumps. Students will be introduced to electrical theory and applications in the piping trades. Students will develop a resume and apply job search techniques. Students who receive a Certificate in Piping Foundation are eligible for credit with the SkilledTradesBC for the first level of technical training in their chosen piping apprenticeship. (Plumber, Steamfitter/Gasfitter, or Sprinkler Fitter) Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

admission.raw: Note: This trade program is in high demand. Visit Trades Training BC to estimate a future start date. Scheduled intakes Multiple start dates each year Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements, we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 11 (50%) or Foundations of Math 11 (50%) or Workplace Math 11 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Trades Discovery The Trades Discovery General and Trades Discovery for Women are full-time programs designed to prepare participants to successfully enter and complete a Trades Training program. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Please note that international students are not eligible to continue to an apprenticeship training program. To learn more about international student opportunities at BCIT, visit BCIT International . Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program does not meet the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is therefore not eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. ( CIPC : 46.0502) Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
